sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《Hidden Brain》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Millions of tweets are posted every day.
sentences.zh: 每天都有数以百万计的推文发布。

sentences.en: Most of them get little attention,
sentences.zh: 其中大多数几乎无人问津，

sentences.en: but there is one user whose tweets always make news.
sentences.zh: 但有一位用户的推文总能成为新闻。

sentences.en: Ding, ding, ding.
sentences.zh: 叮，叮，叮。

sentences.en: There's been a POTUS tweet.
sentences.zh: 总统发推了。

sentences.en: The president is up and tweeting this morning.
sentences.zh: 总统今天早上起床就开始发推了。

sentences.en: He just tweeted two minutes ago this.
sentences.zh: 他两分钟前刚发了这条推文。

sentences.en: He said, I'm extremely pleased to see that CNN
sentences.zh: 他说，我非常高兴地看到美国有线电视新闻网（CNN）

sentences.en: has finally been exposed as fake news and garbage journalism.
sentences.zh: 终于被曝光为假新闻和垃圾新闻。

sentences.en: It's about time.
sentences.zh: 是时候了。

sentences.en: Trump tweeted, quote,
sentences.zh: 特朗普发推称，引用如下：

sentences.en: The United States has foolishly given Pakistan more than $33 billion in aid over the last 15 years,
sentences.zh: 过去15年里，美国愚蠢地向巴基斯坦提供了超过330亿美元的援助，

sentences.en: and they have given us nothing but lies and deceit.
sentences.zh: 而他们给我们的只有谎言和欺骗。

sentences.en: This is not an episode about Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 这并不是一期关于唐纳德·特朗普的节目。

sentences.en: It's an episode about an emotion that predates him, but that he has taken to an extreme.
sentences.zh: 这是一期关于一种先于他存在，但他将其推向极致的情绪的节目。

sentences.en: We now hear this emotion in the way we talk about a broad range of topics.
sentences.zh: 我们现在在谈论广泛话题的方式中都能听到这种情绪。

sentences.en: The emotion is outrage.
sentences.zh: 这种情绪就是愤怒。

sentences.en: With the stench of blatant bias and partisanship surrounding the Russia probe,
sentences.zh: 随着俄罗斯调查周围弥漫着公然偏见和党派之争的恶臭，

sentences.en: It's humiliating to be an American and allowing for this type of behavior to happen.
sentences.zh: 身为美国人却任由这种行为发生，真是令人羞耻。

sentences.en: Vicious, the way she said it.
sentences.zh: 恶毒，她说话的方式真恶毒。

sentences.en: Vicious F-word.
sentences.zh: 恶毒的脏话。

sentences.en: That's not somebody that loves our country.
sentences.zh: 那不是爱我们国家的人。

sentences.en: In the heads of these psychotic Democrats and their friends in the media.
sentences.zh: 在这些精神错乱的民主党人及其媒体朋友的脑子里。

sentences.en: I'm sad.
sentences.zh: 我很伤心。

sentences.en: Sad.
sentences.zh: 悲哀。

sentences.en: We're taught what happened to me.
sentences.zh: 我们被教导了发生在我身上的事。

sentences.en: I'm a seller.
sentences.zh: 我是个推销员。

sentences.en: You are a seller.
sentences.zh: 你是个推销员。

sentences.en: Just like the president, many Americans have come to believe
sentences.zh: 就像总统一样，许多美国人开始相信

sentences.en: that the only way to spur change is by ginning up anger.
sentences.zh: 推动变革的唯一途径就是煽动愤怒。

sentences.en: It isn't enough to say your opponents are wrong.
sentences.zh: 仅仅说你的对手错了是不够的。

sentences.en: You have to say they are reprehensible.
sentences.zh: 你必须说他们是应受谴责的。

sentences.en: This can be for big issues like immigration and health care.
sentences.zh: 这可能针对移民和医疗保健等重大议题。

sentences.en: It can be for smaller issues like the new album by Taylor Swift
sentences.zh: 也可能针对泰勒·斯威夫特的新专辑

sentences.en: or the popularity of Pumpkin Spice.
sentences.zh: 或是南瓜香料的流行等较小议题。

sentences.en: Is all this outrage effective?
sentences.zh: 所有这些愤怒有效吗？

sentences.en: Well, yes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的。

sentences.en: For every moral emotional word that people use in a tweet,
sentences.zh: 对于人们在推文中使用每一个带有道德情感的词汇，

sentences.en: we found that it increased the rate of retweeting
sentences.zh: 我们发现它将转发率提高了

sentences.en: from other people who saw it by 15 to 20 percent.
sentences.zh: 15%到20%，针对的是那些看到推文的其他人。

sentences.en: But it comes at a coSt.
sentences.zh: 但这是有代价的。

sentences.en: Outrage now leaps from our social media feeds and television screens
sentences.zh: 愤怒现在从我们的社交媒体动态和电视屏幕上跳出来，

sentences.en: to PTA meetings and family reunions.
sentences.zh: 蔓延到家长会和家庭聚会中。

sentences.en: Many people feel overwhelmed by the shouting and disengage.
sentences.zh: 许多人感到被喧嚣淹没，从而选择退出。

sentences.en: Others are so consumed with fury
sentences.zh: 另一些人则被愤怒吞噬，

sentences.en: that they become unrecognizable to their friends and neighbors.
sentences.zh: 以至于他们的朋友和邻居都认不出他们了。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain,
sentences.zh: 本周的《Hidden Brain》，

sentences.en: how outrage is hijacking our politics, our communities, and our minds.
sentences.zh: 愤怒是如何劫持我们的政治、社区和思想的。

sentences.en: Saturday, January 19, 2019.
sentences.zh: 2019年1月19日，星期六。

sentences.en: Julie Zimmerman checked Twitter and saw something that made her upset.
sentences.zh: 朱莉·齐默尔曼查看推特时，看到了一些让她心烦意乱的东西。

sentences.en: It was a video filmed hundreds of miles from her home in Ohio
sentences.zh: 那是一段视频，拍摄地点距离她在俄亥俄州的家有数百英里远，

sentences.en: at the National Mall in Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 位于华盛顿特区的国家广场。

sentences.en: There was this older Native American man,
sentences.zh: 视频里有一位年长的美洲原住民男子，

sentences.en: and these kids surrounded him and were yelling things at him
sentences.zh: 这些孩子围着他，对他大喊大叫，

sentences.en: and laughing at him, and they were blocking his path.
sentences.zh: 嘲笑他，还挡住了他的去路。

sentences.en: He apparently was trying to, you know, walk over to the Lincoln Memorial or something like that,
sentences.zh: 他显然是想，你知道，走到林肯纪念堂之类的地方，

sentences.en: and they wouldn't let him through.
sentences.zh: 但他们不让他过去。

sentences.en: The kids surrounding this man looked like 15-year-old boys.
sentences.zh: 围着这个男人的孩子看起来像是15岁的男孩。

sentences.en: They were nearly all white.
sentences.zh: 他们几乎全是白人。

sentences.en: A few were making gestures that looked like tomahawk chops.
sentences.zh: 有几个在做看起来像战斧劈砍的手势。

sentences.en: Some wore hats that read, Make America Great Again.
sentences.zh: 有些人戴着写有“让美国再次伟大”的帽子。

sentences.en: These kids were making fun of this guy because he was Native American,
sentences.zh: 这些孩子嘲笑这个家伙，因为他是美洲原住民，

sentences.en: because he had a drum and was chanting something unfamiliar to them.
sentences.zh: 因为他拿着鼓，还在吟唱一些他们不熟悉的曲调。

sentences.en: It was pretty cringeworthy.
sentences.zh: 这真是让人尴尬得要命。

sentences.en: We're going to look at Julie's encounter with the story in some detail
sentences.zh: 我们将详细审视朱莉对这个故事的接触，

sentences.en: because it's revealing about how outrage works today.
sentences.zh: 因为它揭示了当今愤怒是如何运作的。

sentences.en: Like many others watching that day, Julie fixated on one boy in the video.
sentences.zh: 像那天观看视频的许多其他人一样，朱莉盯着视频里的一个男孩。

sentences.en: He was standing directly in front of the Native American man, staring at him.
sentences.zh: 他站在美洲原住民男子正前方，盯着他看。

sentences.en: He had what looked like a smirk on his face,
sentences.zh: 他脸上带着一种看起来像是假笑的表情，

sentences.en: as the older man sang.
sentences.zh: 当时那位老人正在唱歌。

sentences.en: His image evoked all the horrifying things
sentences.zh: 他的形象唤起了几个世纪以来

sentences.en: Americans have done to Native Americans
sentences.zh: 美国人对美洲原住民所做的

sentences.en: throughout the centuries.
sentences.zh: 所有可怕的事情。

sentences.en: As the day went on, more details emerged.
sentences.zh: 随着时间推移，更多细节浮出水面。

sentences.en: The boys were students at Covington Catholic High School
sentences.zh: 这些男孩是肯塔基州卡温顿天主教高中的学生，

sentences.en: in Kentucky, just across the river from Cincinnati,
sentences.zh: 就在辛辛那提河对岸，

sentences.en: where Julie lives.
sentences.zh: 朱莉就住在那里。

sentences.en: I started seeing tweets that the kids were chanting,
sentences.zh: 我开始看到推文说孩子们在喊，

sentences.en: build the wall, build that wall.
sentences.zh: “建墙，建那堵墙”。

sentences.en: Julie's son was around the same age
sentences.zh: 朱莉的儿子和视频里的孩子

sentences.en: as the kids in the video,
sentences.zh: 年龄差不多，

sentences.en: And he also went to a Catholic school.
sentences.zh: 而且他也上天主教学校。

sentences.en: Julie texted him.
sentences.zh: 朱莉给他发了短信。

sentences.en: I said, you know, if I ever caught you acting that way,
sentences.zh: 我说，你知道，如果我发现你那样做，

sentences.en: I mean, I'd be horrified.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我会感到震惊。

sentences.en: By the evening,
sentences.zh: 到了晚上，

sentences.en: Now to the outrage over a video showing...
sentences.zh: 现在转向关于一段视频的愤怒，视频显示……

sentences.en: The story was everywhere.
sentences.zh: 这个故事无处不在。

sentences.en: By now it's likely that you've seen this...
sentences.zh: 到现在你很可能已经看过这个了……

sentences.en: You've probably seen it by now.
sentences.zh: 你现在可能已经看过了。

sentences.en: The viral video sweeping the internet
sentences.zh: 席卷互联网的病毒式视频，

sentences.en: of a mob of MAGA hat-wearing high school students.
sentences.zh: 关于一群戴着“让美国再次伟大”帽子的高中生。

sentences.en: A troubling scene many are calling a racist
sentences.zh: 许多人称之为种族主义的令人不安的场景，

sentences.en: played out in Washington yesterday
sentences.zh: 昨天在华盛顿上演。

sentences.en: Clearly these boys are not getting a good education because it makes little sense to angrily chant build the wall to a population with literally zero illegal immigrants who were here long before we were.
sentences.zh: 显然这些男孩没有受到良好的教育，因为对着一个人口中非法移民为零，且比我们早到这里很久的人愤怒地高喊“建墙”，这毫无意义。

sentences.en: I talked to a friend of mine who lives in New York, a former roommate of mine, and she said her yoga teacher called and said, let's drive to that school in Kentucky and proteSt.
sentences.zh: 我和一位住在纽约的朋友，也就是我以前的室友谈过，她说她的瑜伽老师打电话说，让我们开车去肯塔基州那所学校抗议。

sentences.en: Like, that's the sort of level of reaction people were having to this.
sentences.zh: 就像，人们对这件事的反应就是这种程度。

sentences.en: Like, this yoga teacher in New York wanted to hop in the car and drive 10 hours to protest in front of the school.
sentences.zh: 就像，这位纽约的瑜伽老师想跳上车，开10个小时的车去学校门前抗议。

sentences.en: While Julie's friends were texting her messages of outrage, her son was having very different conversations about the same video.
sentences.zh: 当朱莉的朋友们给她发愤怒的信息时，她的儿子正在就同一段视频进行非常不同的对话。

sentences.en: His friends had started texting him at some point on Saturday,
sentences.zh: 他的朋友们在周六的某个时候开始给他发短信，

sentences.en: saying, you know, I think that these guys are getting a bum rap.
sentences.zh: 说，你知道，我觉得这些人被冤枉了。

sentences.en: I don't think they're guilty of what they're being accused of.
sentences.zh: 我不认为他们犯了被指控的那些罪行。

sentences.en: Sunday, January 20th, 2019.
sentences.zh: 2019年1月20日，星期日。

sentences.en: In the late morning, after church, Julie checked Twitter.
sentences.zh: 周日上午晚些时候，礼拜结束后，朱莉查看了推特。

sentences.en: She saw that someone had uploaded a nearly two-hour-long video
sentences.zh: 她看到有人上传了一段近两小时长的视频，

sentences.en: which showed much more of the confrontation
sentences.zh: 展示了天主教学校学生与美洲原住民男子之间

sentences.en: between the Catholic school students and the Native American man.
sentences.zh: 冲突的更多细节。

sentences.en: I started watching because I wanted to show my son
sentences.zh: 我开始观看，因为我想向我儿子展示

sentences.en: where the kids had been chanting, build the wall.
sentences.zh: 孩子们在哪里喊过“建墙”。

sentences.en: He challenged me on that point,
sentences.zh: 他反驳了我的观点，

sentences.en: and I watched the hour-plus video of the incident,
sentences.zh: 我看了那段一个多小时的事件视频，

sentences.en: and I couldn't find anywhere where they had been chanting that.
sentences.zh: 我找不到任何他们喊过那个口号的地方。

sentences.en: And that wasn't all.
sentences.zh: 而且还不止这些。

sentences.en: This is what the longer video showed.
sentences.zh: 这就是较长视频显示的内容。

sentences.en: The kids were on the mall for the annual March for Life, which is an anti-abortion march that happens every year in January.
sentences.zh: 孩子们在广场上参加一年一度的“为生命而行”活动，这是一个每年一月举行的反堕胎游行。

sentences.en: It was right before Martin Luther King Day.
sentences.zh: 就在马丁·路德·金纪念日之前。

sentences.en: The mall was packed.
sentences.zh: 广场上挤满了人。

sentences.en: There was a group called the Black Hebrew Israelites, and they were yelling vile things at the kids.
sentences.zh: 有一个叫“黑人希伯来以色列人”的团体，他们对孩子们大喊恶毒的话。

sentences.en: A bunch of babies made out of insects.
sentences.zh: 一群由昆虫组成的婴儿。

sentences.en: You know, somebody yelling something at you doesn't give you justification to yell anything back.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有人对你大喊大叫并不能成为你回击任何话的理由。

sentences.en: But I thought that set a tone that these kids, some of whom may have never been in a situation like this, might have been feeling nervous or attacked or I don't know.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这定下了一个基调，这些孩子，其中一些人可能从未处于过这样的境地，可能感到紧张或受到攻击，或者我不知道。

sentences.en: So the insults being yelled by the Black Hebrew Israelites
sentences.zh: 所以“黑人希伯来以色列人”喊出的侮辱性言语

sentences.en: definitely altered my understanding of what happened next.
sentences.zh: 确实改变了我对接下来发生事情的理解。

sentences.en: The Indigenous People's March was also taking place in D.C.
sentences.zh: “原住民游行”当天也在华盛顿举行。

sentences.en: that day.
sentences.zh: 那天。

sentences.en: Nathan Phillips was the older man in the original viral video.
sentences.zh: 内森·菲利普斯是最初病毒式视频中的那位老人。

sentences.en: I saw Phillips walk over to the kids on this longer video.
sentences.zh: 我在这个较长的视频中看到菲利普斯走向孩子们。

sentences.en: And remember, the original video had just shown Phillips surrounded by these kids.
sentences.zh: 记住，最初的视频只是显示菲利普斯被这些孩子包围了。

sentences.en: And the extrapolation originally was that these kids had walked up to Phillips and surrounded him and blocked his path and not allowed him to pass.
sentences.zh: 最初的推断是这些孩子走到菲利普斯面前包围了他，挡住了他的去路，不让他通过。

sentences.en: Well, as you watch the longer video, you see Phillips and an entourage.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当你观看较长的视频时，你会看到菲利普斯和一群随从。

sentences.en: I mean, there were a lot of people with Phillips all walking over to talk to the kids.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有很多人和菲利普斯一起走过去和孩子们说话。

sentences.en: So Phillips had not been trying to get somewhere, and these kids blocked him.
sentences.zh: 所以菲利普斯并不是想去某个地方，然后被这些孩子挡住了。

sentences.en: He actually went up and initiated the interaction with the kids.
sentences.zh: 实际上是他走过去主动发起了与孩子们的互动。

sentences.en: And what were the kids doing?
sentences.zh: 孩子们在做什么？

sentences.en: What were they chanting?
sentences.zh: 他们在喊什么？

sentences.en: What were they shouting?
sentences.zh: 他们在叫什么？

sentences.en: Some of them were trying to make their friends laugh.
sentences.zh: 他们中的一些人试图逗朋友笑。

sentences.en: Some of them were being offensive.
sentences.zh: 他们中的一些人表现得很有冒犯性。

sentences.en: I think, you know, doing a tomahawk chop is an offensive thing to do.
sentences.zh: 我想，你知道，做战斧劈砍动作是一件冒犯人的事情。

sentences.en: And the student who was smirking at Nathan Phillips?
sentences.zh: 至于那个对着内森·菲利普斯假笑的学生？

sentences.en: He was laughing for a while, and then they kind of locked eyes.
sentences.zh: 他笑了一会儿，然后他们对视了。

sentences.en: And I don't know what he was thinking.
sentences.zh: 我不知道他在想什么。

sentences.en: I don't know what he was feeling.
sentences.zh: 我不知道他在感受什么。

sentences.en: But I've seen that look on teenagers where you've got waves of thoughts passing through your head,
sentences.zh: 但我见过青少年那种神情，脑海中闪过一波又一波的想法，

sentences.en: and your underlying thinking is, what do I do?
sentences.zh: 你内心深处的想法是，我该怎么办？

sentences.en: I don't know what to do.
sentences.zh: 我不知道该怎么办。

sentences.en: You know, he looked nervous to me.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在我看来他看起来很紧张。

sentences.en: Julie had seen the smirking boy as emblematic of the terrible things done to Native Americans.
sentences.zh: 朱莉曾将那个假笑的男孩视为美洲原住民所受可怕待遇的象征。

sentences.en: Now, she saw a teenager who was trying hard not to show his friends that he was nervous.
sentences.zh: 当时，她看到一个少年正极力掩饰自己的紧张，不想让朋友们看出来。

sentences.en: On social and broadcast media, the outrage flipped.
sentences.zh: 在社交媒体和广播媒体上，舆论风向发生了逆转。

sentences.en: If you were left-leaning, you were outraged by these kids.
sentences.zh: 如果你倾向左翼，你就会对这些孩子感到愤怒。

sentences.en: Originally, if you were conservative, you just put your head under a rock
sentences.zh: 起初，如果你是保守派，你只会躲起来，

sentences.en: because even you couldn't defend what you originally saw.
sentences.zh: 因为连你自己都无法为最初看到的那一幕辩护。

sentences.en: Then there was a reaction to it where a lot of conservatives, after they had seen the longer video, started defending these kids.
sentences.zh: 随后，舆论出现了反弹，许多保守派在看过完整视频后，开始为这些孩子辩护。

sentences.en: And what was interesting to me was how difficult it was for people to change their original take on it.
sentences.zh: 令我感兴趣的是，人们想要改变最初的看法竟是如此困难。

sentences.en: I was afraid to tell a few people initially that I had changed my mind about the Covington Catholic thing, which is crazy.
sentences.zh: 起初我甚至不敢告诉别人我已经改变了对“科文顿天主教高中事件”的看法，这简直太疯狂了。

sentences.en: Like, why can't you just say, you know, I think I was wrong about this.
sentences.zh: 就像是，为什么你就不能直接说，你知道吗，我觉得我在这件事上错了。

sentences.en: But I knew some people would be upset because it's as though you're giving your enemy ammunition by admitting that they might be right and you might have been wrong.
sentences.zh: 但我知道有些人会不高兴，因为承认对方可能是对的、而自己可能是错的，就好像是在给敌人递刀子。

sentences.en: And you can't ever show weakness or, you know, admit that maybe the other side has a point.
sentences.zh: 你永远不能表现出软弱，或者承认对方可能有道理。

sentences.en: Julie told a friend about her change of heart, and her friend encouraged her to write an essay
sentences.zh: 朱莉把她心态的转变告诉了一位朋友，朋友鼓励她写一篇文章

sentences.en: about it.

sentences.en: And I wrote that essay probably in 15 minutes.
sentences.zh: 我大概只花了15分钟就写完了那篇文章。

sentences.en: I mean, it just spilled out.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它就像泉水一样涌了出来。

sentences.en: And I submitted it for publication, and it was published very quickly.
sentences.zh: 我把它投给了出版机构，很快就发表了。

sentences.en: The essay was published in The Atlantic.
sentences.zh: 这篇文章发表在《大西洋》杂志上。

sentences.en: The headline read,
sentences.zh: 标题写着：

sentences.zh: “我没能通过科文顿天主教高中的考验”。在文中，朱莉承认自己当时太草率，

sentences.en: quick to judgment.
sentences.zh: 太急于下结论了。

sentences.en: Almost immediately after her essay was posted, it prompted howls of outrage
sentences.zh: 文章发布后几乎立刻引起了轩然大波，

sentences.en: from the right.
sentences.zh: 来自右翼的愤怒声讨接踵而至。

sentences.en: My essay was weaponized against liberals, against progressives.
sentences.zh: 我的文章被当作武器，用来攻击自由派和进步派。

sentences.en: And I, you know,
sentences.zh: 而我，你知道，

sentences.en: it made me uncomfortable to see that, like, oh gosh, did I make a mistake here?
sentences.zh: 看到这些让我感到不安，心想，天哪，我是不是犯了个错？

sentences.en: My brother-in-law
sentences.zh: 我的妹夫

sentences.en: called my husband to say, Rush Limbaugh just mentioned your wife's name on the air.
sentences.zh: 给我丈夫打电话说，拉什·林博刚才在广播里提到了你妻子的名字。

sentences.en: And I
sentences.zh: 而我

sentences.zh: 心想，天哪，我到底做了什么？

sentences.zh: 那些真正把科文顿这些孩子

sentences.en: kids from Covington was at the Atlantic.
sentences.zh: 架在火上烤的“免下车”媒体之一，就是《大西洋》杂志。

sentences.en: And a writer at the Atlantic has published a piece,
sentences.zh: 而《大西洋》的一位作者发表了一篇文章，

sentences.en: I failed the Covington Catholic teSt. Next time there's a viral story, I'll wait for more facts
sentences.zh: 标题是“我没能通过科文顿天主教高中的考验”。下次再有病毒式传播的故事，我会等更多事实

sentences.en: to emerge.
sentences.zh: 浮出水面再做评价。

sentences.en: Julie Irwin Zimmerman.
sentences.zh: 朱莉·欧文·齐默尔曼。

sentences.en: She was one of the early pilers on, and she's begging forgiveness.
sentences.zh: 她是当初最早参与围攻的人之一，现在却在乞求原谅。

sentences.en: She failed the teSt. She went along with what?
sentences.zh: 她没通过考验。她当时随大流做了什么？

sentences.en: Why does anybody in their right mind, I know the
sentences.zh: 为什么任何一个理智的人——我知道这种诱惑很大——在社交媒体上的任何内容

sentences.en: temptation, but why isn't there even a moment's pause when anything from social media becomes
sentences.zh: 成为“免下车”媒体的素材来源时，

sentences.en: source material in drive-by media?
sentences.zh: 甚至不能停下来思考片刻呢？

sentences.en: It is a cesspool and everybody knows that it's a cesspool.
sentences.zh: 那是个污水坑，每个人都知道那是污水坑。

sentences.en: Rush Limbaugh was wrong in several ways.
sentences.zh: 拉什·林博在几个方面都错了。

sentences.en: Julie didn't work at the Atlantic and had nothing to
sentences.zh: 朱莉并不在《大西洋》工作，也与他们最初的报道

sentences.en: do with their initial coverage.
sentences.zh: 毫无关系。

sentences.en: And she was not an early piler on.
sentences.zh: 而且她也不是最早参与围攻的人。

sentences.en: Before she wrote her essay,
sentences.zh: 在她写那篇文章之前，

sentences.en: she herself had posted nothing on social media about the Covington Catholic students.
sentences.zh: 她自己从未在社交媒体上发布过任何关于科文顿天主教高中学生的内容。

sentences.en: In addition, lots of journalists had, in fact, covered the story with nuance.
sentences.zh: 此外，事实上有很多记者在报道这个故事时都保持了细致入微的态度。

sentences.en: Ironically,
sentences.zh: 讽刺的是，

sentences.en: Rush Limbaugh was doing exactly what Julie had initially done.
sentences.zh: 拉什·林博所做的正是朱莉最初做过的事。

sentences.en: He was leaping to sweeping
sentences.zh: 他仅凭极其有限的证据，就对自由派、对朱莉、对记者

sentences.en: conclusions about liberals, about Julie, about journalists, with very limited evidence.
sentences.zh: 做出了以偏概全的结论。

sentences.en: This is the way our cycles of outrage work.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们愤怒循环的运作方式。

sentences.en: Each blast produces misstatements, exaggerations, and errors.
sentences.zh: 每一次爆发都会产生失实、夸大和错误。

sentences.en: These are then seized upon by the other side,
sentences.zh: 这些错误随后被另一方抓住，

sentences.en: which proceeds to produce its own misstatements, exaggerations, and errors.
sentences.zh: 进而产生他们自己的失实、夸大和错误。

sentences.en: The cycle feeds on itself.
sentences.zh: 这个循环在自我滋养。

sentences.en: The outrage in the Covington Catholic School scandal is emblematic of our times.
sentences.zh: 科文顿天主教高中丑闻中的愤怒，正是我们这个时代的缩影。

sentences.en: Right-wing talk radio invented the modern art of the rant.
sentences.zh: 右翼谈话广播发明了现代咆哮艺术。

sentences.en: Cable television pundits perfected it.
sentences.zh: 有线电视评论员完善了它。

sentences.en: Social media has made outrage part of daily discourse.
sentences.zh: 社交媒体则让愤怒成为了日常对话的一部分。

sentences.en: Now, instead of a handful of screaming voices on radio and TV,
sentences.zh: 现在，不再仅仅是广播和电视上那几个尖叫的声音，

sentences.en: you have thousands of people, on the right and the left,
sentences.zh: 而是成千上万的人，无论左右，

sentences.en: enraged about politics and each other.
sentences.zh: 都对政治和彼此感到愤怒。

sentences.en: Events that would never have been considered news stories
sentences.zh: 那些原本根本不会被视为新闻事件的事情，

sentences.en: now dominate the headlines.
sentences.zh: 现在却占据了头条。

sentences.en: Julie used to be a reporter and editorial writer at the Cincinnati Enquirer.
sentences.zh: 朱莉曾是《辛辛那提问询报》的记者和社论撰稿人。

sentences.en: If you were my editor and I came to you and said,
sentences.zh: 如果你是我的编辑，我跑去跟你说：

sentences.en: yeah, this Native American guy and these kids in MAGA hats
sentences.zh: “嘿，今天在商场里，这个美洲原住民男子和这些戴着‘让美国再次伟大’帽子的孩子

sentences.en: kind of got in this tense standoff on the mall today,
sentences.zh: 陷入了紧张的对峙，

sentences.en: and I think it's a story.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是个新闻。”

sentences.en: Any self-respecting editor would say, you know, did somebody get shot?
sentences.zh: 任何一个有自尊的编辑都会问：“有人中枪了吗？”

sentences.en: You know, how is this a story?
sentences.zh: “这算哪门子新闻？”

sentences.en: This weird confrontations between people happen all the time,
sentences.zh: 这种人与人之间奇怪的冲突时有发生，

sentences.en: and we don't consider them to be news stories.
sentences.zh: 我们通常不会把它们当作新闻报道。

sentences.en: But the ground rules have changed.
sentences.zh: 但游戏规则已经变了。

sentences.en: All of a sudden, there are powerful incentives
sentences.zh: 突然之间，人们有了强大的动力

sentences.en: to be fastest to react and loudest to shout.
sentences.zh: 去争做反应最快、嗓门最大的人。

sentences.en: People are falling all over each other
sentences.zh: 人们争先恐后地

sentences.en: to be first in line to say how awful this was.
sentences.zh: 排队去表达这件事有多么糟糕。

sentences.en: You get to show how woke you are
sentences.zh: 你借此展示自己的“觉醒”程度，

sentences.en: or how conservative you are
sentences.zh: 或者展示自己有多么保守，

sentences.en: without actually doing any work.
sentences.zh: 却根本不需要做任何实际工作。

sentences.en: You just look at something, you retweet it,
sentences.zh: 你只是看了一眼，转发一下，

sentences.en: You try to make a really smart, funny comment that thousands of people will retweet.
sentences.zh: 试着写一条看起来很聪明、很幽默的评论，好让成千上万的人转发。

sentences.en: And then you kind of pat yourself on the back for being involved in the conversation.
sentences.zh: 然后你就可以因为参与了这场对话而沾沾自喜。

sentences.en: But you have done nothing.
sentences.zh: 但你其实什么都没做。

sentences.en: Is Julie right?
sentences.zh: 朱莉说得对吗？

sentences.en: Is all this anger really accomplishing nothing?
sentences.zh: 所有这些愤怒真的什么都没改变吗？

sentences.en: What researchers have found about the science of viral outrage when we come back.
sentences.zh: 当我们回来时，将探讨研究人员关于病毒式愤怒科学的发现。

sentences.en: Cast your mind back to a party.
sentences.zh: 回想一下某个聚会。

sentences.en: One that happened a long, long time ago.
sentences.zh: 一个很久很久以前发生的聚会。

sentences.en: Someone at this party does something bad, maybe steals something.
sentences.zh: 聚会上有人做了坏事，也许是偷了东西。

sentences.en: The group has to decide what to do with this lawbreaker.
sentences.zh: 群体必须决定如何处置这个违规者。

sentences.en: Do nothing, and the transgressor might do bad stuff again.
sentences.zh: 什么都不做，违规者可能会再次作恶。

sentences.en: Better to punish him or cast him out.
sentences.zh: 最好惩罚他或把他驱逐出去。

sentences.en: Over thousands of generations, humans learned that punishing bad behavior accomplished useful things.
sentences.zh: 经过数千代的演化，人类认识到惩罚不良行为能带来有益的结果。

sentences.en: It's like evolution placed a bet on that being a good idea for the group.
sentences.zh: 就像进化论押注这对群体来说是个好主意。

sentences.en: This is Yale psychologist Molly Crockett.
sentences.zh: 这是耶鲁大学心理学家莫莉·克罗克特。

sentences.en: Molly says outrage about wrongdoing and the punishments it produced kept people in line.
sentences.zh: 莫莉说，对不当行为的愤怒及其产生的惩罚，能让人们守规矩。

sentences.en: This was good for the group.
sentences.zh: 这对群体有好处。

sentences.en: It also happened to be good for individuals.
sentences.zh: 碰巧这对个人也有好处。

sentences.en: Our brains evolved to give us a little boost when we get outraged and punish someone.
sentences.zh: 我们的大脑进化出了一种机制：当我们感到愤怒并惩罚某人时，会获得一点快感。

sentences.en: When people decide to punish somebody who's behaved unfairly,
sentences.zh: 当人们决定惩罚那些行为不公的人时，

sentences.en: we see activation in brain areas associated with reward,
sentences.zh: 我们观察到大脑中与奖励相关的区域会被激活，

sentences.en: including the serratum and the medial prefrontal cortex.
sentences.zh: 包括纹状体和内侧前额叶皮层。

sentences.en: In layman's terms, calling out another person's bad behavior feels good.
sentences.zh: 用通俗的话说，指出别人的不良行为感觉很爽。

sentences.en: Molly and her team have conducted experiments
sentences.zh: 莫莉和她的团队进行了实验，

sentences.en: where they ask volunteers to play the role of a punisher.
sentences.zh: 他们让志愿者扮演惩罚者的角色。

sentences.en: When the volunteer sees something unfair,
sentences.zh: 当志愿者看到不公平的事情时，

sentences.en: she can punish the person responsible.
sentences.zh: 她可以惩罚责任人。

sentences.en: Molly says people asked to play the role of punisher
sentences.zh: 莫莉说，被要求扮演惩罚者角色的人，

sentences.en: are not only willing to penalize wrongdoers,
sentences.zh: 不仅愿意惩罚违规者，

sentences.en: but to make personal sacrifices in order to do so.
sentences.zh: 甚至愿意为此做出个人牺牲。

sentences.en: For example, in one experiment,
sentences.zh: 例如，在一个实验中，

sentences.en: the punisher sees that someone has divided a pot of money unfairly
sentences.zh: 惩罚者看到有人不公平地瓜分了一笔钱，

sentences.en: rather than share it equitably with another person.
sentences.zh: 而不是与他人公平分享。

sentences.en: I can spend some money to burn your money,
sentences.zh: 我可以花钱来烧掉你的钱，

sentences.en: and you get sent a message saying that that happened,
sentences.zh: 你会收到一条消息说发生了这种事，

sentences.en: and you get a final payoff,
sentences.zh: 你会得到最终的报酬，

sentences.en: and you learn how big it could have been
sentences.zh: 并且你会知道如果我没有烧掉你的一些钱，

sentences.en: if I hadn't burned some of your money.
sentences.zh: 你本可以得到多少。

sentences.en: In this rational model of punishment,
sentences.zh: 在这种理性的惩罚模型中，

sentences.en: wrongdoers know they are being punished.
sentences.zh: 违规者知道自己正在受到惩罚。

sentences.en: In fact, it is this knowledge
sentences.zh: 事实上，正是这种认知

sentences.en: that is supposed to act as a deterrent.
sentences.zh: 被认为起到了威慑作用。

sentences.en: But Molly and her team asked a deeper question.
sentences.zh: 但莫莉和她的团队提出了一个更深层的问题。

sentences.en: Would volunteers also be willing to punish transgressors
sentences.zh: 志愿者是否也愿意惩罚那些

sentences.en: who don't get told they are being punished?
sentences.zh: 根本不知道自己正在受到惩罚的违规者？

sentences.en: The only reason why I would punish you
sentences.zh: 我之所以会在暗中惩罚你，

sentences.en: when it's in secret
sentences.zh: 唯一的原因就是，

sentences.en: is if I get some personal satisfaction
sentences.zh: 当我得知你作为一个不公平的人最终得到的钱变少了，

sentences.en: from knowing that you, as an unfair person, end up with less money.
sentences.zh: 我会获得某种个人满足感。

sentences.en: Even when transgressors had no idea they were being punished,
sentences.zh: 即使违规者根本不知道自己受到了惩罚，

sentences.en: when they didn't know how much they would have received otherwise,
sentences.zh: 即使他们不知道如果不被惩罚本可以得到多少钱，

sentences.en: Molly found that punishers were more than happy to mete out justice.
sentences.zh: 莫莉发现，惩罚者依然非常乐于伸张正义。

sentences.en: There's a sort of visceral satisfaction in doling out punishment,
sentences.zh: 实施惩罚有一种发自内心的满足感，

sentences.en: and this is corroborated by the brain imaging evidence,
sentences.zh: 这一点得到了脑成像证据的证实，

sentences.en: which shows that when we decide to punish,
sentences.zh: 证据显示，当我们决定惩罚时，

sentences.en: we see activation in brain areas associated with reward.
sentences.zh: 大脑中与奖励相关的区域会被激活。

sentences.en: Outrage, in other words, has been so valuable in our evolutionary history
sentences.zh: 换句话说，愤怒在我们的进化史上非常有价值，

sentences.en: that it operates like other important biological functions.
sentences.zh: 以至于它像其他重要的生物功能一样运作。

sentences.en: It gives us pleasure.
sentences.zh: 它能给我们带来快感。

sentences.en: But here's the thing.
sentences.zh: 但问题在于，

sentences.en: Remember the context in which outrage evolved.
sentences.zh: 记住愤怒进化的背景。

sentences.en: It evolved in an environment where we interacted with people face-to-face,
sentences.zh: 它进化于一个我们面对面互动的环境，

sentences.en: in small groups, in situations where we're going to repeatedly interact with the same people.
sentences.zh: 在小群体中，在我们需要与同一些人反复打交道的情况下。

sentences.en: In this context, outrage produced benefits,
sentences.zh: 在这种背景下，愤怒产生了益处，

sentences.en: but it also came with costs that prompted people to be judicious about it.
sentences.zh: 但也伴随着代价，这促使人们对此保持审慎。

sentences.en: If your neighbor, Og, stole someone's food and you vented your anger at him,
sentences.zh: 如果你的邻居奥格偷了别人的食物，而你对他发泄了怒火，

sentences.en: it might feel good, but it could also be dangerous.
sentences.zh: 这感觉可能不错，但也可能很危险。

sentences.en: Og could get mad at you, punch you in the throat.
sentences.zh: 奥格可能会对你发火，然后朝你喉咙来上一拳。

sentences.en: You would have to judge when and where and how much it made sense to express outrage.
sentences.zh: 你得自己判断在何时、何地以及在多大程度上表达愤怒是合理的。

sentences.en: What happens when we take an emotion carefully calibrated for small net groups
sentences.zh: 当我们把一种针对小规模群体而精心校准的情绪，

sentences.en: and give it a global platform.
sentences.zh: 放到一个全球性的平台上时，会发生什么呢？

sentences.en: It's not very well equipped for the environment in which we find ourselves now,
sentences.zh: 它并不太适应我们现在所处的环境，

sentences.en: where the audience is much, much bigger than it traditionally has been.
sentences.zh: 因为现在的受众比过去要庞大得多。

sentences.en: Now I can be angry at total strangers half a world away,
sentences.zh: 现在，我可以对远在半个地球之外的陌生人感到愤怒，

sentences.en: and my physical costs of expressing that outrage?
sentences.zh: 而我表达这种愤怒的身体成本呢？

sentences.en: Close to zero.
sentences.zh: 几乎为零。

sentences.en: Given that the psychological benefits are high and the physical costs are low,
sentences.zh: 鉴于心理收益很高，而身体成本很低，

sentences.en: there are few checks on outrage anymore.
sentences.zh: 愤怒几乎不再受到任何制约。

sentences.en: This is why many of us today feel surrounded by outrage.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们许多人今天感到被愤怒所包围。

sentences.en: It's nearly impossible to escape.
sentences.zh: 几乎无处可逃。

sentences.en: Molly has noticed something else.
sentences.zh: 莫莉还注意到了另一件事。

sentences.en: Many of us don't want to escape the vitriol.
sentences.zh: 我们许多人并不想逃离这种尖酸刻薄。

sentences.en: People on both the right and left revel in it.
sentences.zh: 无论左右派，人们都沉溺其中。

sentences.en: As a user of social media, one thing that I noticed in my own behavior, particularly after the 2016 elections,
sentences.zh: 作为一名社交媒体用户，我注意到自己行为中的一件事，特别是在2016年大选之后，

sentences.en: was just how much more time I was spending online and particularly how I felt myself getting sucked into feedback loops where I would read something,
sentences.zh: 就是我花在网上的时间多了很多，尤其是当我感到自己陷入了反馈循环：读到一些东西，

sentences.en: I would feel outraged about it, I would feel compelled to share it with my friends.
sentences.zh: 我会感到愤怒，并觉得有必要把它分享给朋友。

sentences.en: I would then be sort of obsessively checking to see whether people had responded,
sentences.zh: 然后我会有点强迫性地去查看人们是否做出了回应，

sentences.en: how they had responded, you know, lather, rinse, repeat.
sentences.zh: 他们是如何回应的，你知道的，周而复始，乐此不疲。

sentences.en: Every time Molly plugged herself into circuits of outrage,
sentences.zh: 每当莫莉接入愤怒的回路，

sentences.en: every time she fired off a zinger about President Trump,
sentences.zh: 每当她针对特朗普总统发出一句尖刻的讽刺，

sentences.en: the ancient circuits in her brain gave her a little reward.
sentences.zh: 她大脑中古老的回路就会给她一点奖励。

sentences.en: Fast forward to early 2017.
sentences.zh: 快进到2017年初。

sentences.en: President Donald Trump's executive order barring many foreigners,
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统签署行政令，禁止许多外国人，

sentences.en: including all refugees from entering the U.S.
sentences.zh: 包括所有难民进入美国，

sentences.en: caused confusion at airports around the world.
sentences.zh: 这在世界各地的机场引发了混乱。

sentences.en: The Trump administration began advancing a series of anti-immigration measures.
sentences.zh: 特朗普政府开始推行一系列反移民措施。

sentences.en: A friend of mine shared an article that the story was about something like the economic benefits of immigrants
sentences.zh: 我的一位朋友分享了一篇文章，内容大概是关于移民的经济效益，

sentences.en: and how farms in California were seeing tomatoes rot on the vine
sentences.zh: 以及加州的农场如何眼睁睁看着番茄烂在藤上，

sentences.en: because they couldn't find enough workers to harvest those tomatoes.
sentences.zh: 因为他们找不到足够的工人来采摘。

sentences.en: And I read this.
sentences.zh: 我读了这篇文章。

sentences.en: I was outraged.
sentences.zh: 我感到很愤怒。

sentences.en: I shared it.
sentences.zh: 我分享了它。

sentences.en: And then a lot of my friends liked it.
sentences.zh: 然后我的很多朋友都点了赞。

sentences.en: And then I got a comment from someone that I didn't even really know that well.
sentences.zh: 接着我收到了一条评论，来自一个我甚至不太熟的人。

sentences.en: And they said the date of this article is 2011.
sentences.zh: 他们说这篇文章的日期是2011年。

sentences.en: The president at that time was not Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 当时的总统不是唐纳德·特朗普，

sentences.en: but someone Molly admired, Barack Obama.
sentences.zh: 而是莫莉所钦佩的巴拉克·奥巴马。

sentences.en: Molly quietly deleted the Facebook poSt.
sentences.zh: 莫莉默默地删除了那条Facebook帖子。

sentences.en: But the incident was a wake-up call.
sentences.zh: 但这件事是一个警钟。

sentences.en: She looked back on her behavior,
sentences.zh: 她回顾了自己的行为，

sentences.en: how she would get lost in a world of posts, shares, and likes.
sentences.zh: 回顾了自己是如何迷失在帖子、分享和点赞的世界里的。

sentences.en: It was like coming out of a trance
sentences.zh: 那感觉就像从恍惚中醒来，

sentences.en: and having this realization that time had disappeared
sentences.zh: 意识到时间已经消失了，

sentences.en: and that I had been engaged in a feedback loop,
sentences.zh: 而我一直沉浸在一个反馈循环中，

sentences.en: Not unlike the apparatus that my PhD lab used to train rats to press leavers to get cocaine, literally.
sentences.zh: 这和我的博士实验室用来训练老鼠按杠杆获取可卡因的装置没什么两样，真的。

sentences.en: Like, I'm not saying that social media is cocaine.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我并不是在说社交媒体就是可卡因。

sentences.en: I think there are actually really important distinctions between substance addiction and social media use, and they get conflated a lot in the media.
sentences.zh: 我认为物质成瘾和社交媒体使用之间确实存在非常重要的区别，媒体经常把它们混为一谈。

sentences.en: But one thread that they have in common is that both of these processes do seem to tap into our reinforcement learning circuitry in the brain.
sentences.zh: 但它们共同的一点是，这两个过程似乎都触及了我们大脑中的强化学习回路。

sentences.en: Most of us underestimate how powerful this brain circuitry can be,
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人都低估了这种大脑回路的强大程度，

sentences.en: how vulnerable we are to the psychological rewards that come from feeling really, truly mad about something,
sentences.zh: 低估了我们对那种因对某事感到真正愤怒，

sentences.en: and then seeing our outrage amplified by others.
sentences.zh: 并看到我们的愤怒被他人放大而产生的心理奖励是多么脆弱。

sentences.en: Social rewards are just as powerful, if not more powerful, in driving learning and decision making than chocolate or money, right?
sentences.zh: 社交奖励在驱动学习和决策方面，即使不比巧克力或金钱更强大，也同样强大，对吧？

sentences.en: The approval of our peers is like the most potent reward you can get for social beings like us.
sentences.zh: 对于像我们这样的社会性生物来说，同伴的认可可能是你能得到的最强有力的奖励。

sentences.en: Social media platforms take our love for this kind of approval and pour rocket fuel on it.
sentences.zh: 社交媒体平台利用我们对这种认可的渴望，并为其注入了火箭燃料。

sentences.en: When you shared a story with a group of friends in the days before social media,
sentences.zh: 在社交媒体出现之前的日子里，当你和一群朋友分享一个故事时，

sentences.en: you might not know exactly what they thought of it.
sentences.zh: 你可能并不确切知道他们对此有何看法。

sentences.en: You had to watch their faces.
sentences.zh: 你必须观察他们的表情。

sentences.en: And even then, the responses might be ambiguous.
sentences.zh: 即便如此，他们的反应也可能是模糊的。

sentences.en: But these days?
sentences.zh: 但现在呢？

sentences.en: Now we get a count.
sentences.zh: 现在我们有了计数。

sentences.en: We can see, oh, 10 friends liked that article I shared.
sentences.zh: 我们可以看到，哦，有10个朋友点赞了我分享的那篇文章。

sentences.en: But the one I shared yesterday got 70 likes.
sentences.zh: 但我昨天分享的那篇获得了70个赞。

sentences.en: So these are signals that we can use to tune our behavior.
sentences.zh: 所以这些是我们用来调整行为的信号。

sentences.en: And we have quantified social feedback now in a way that was much more vague before social media.
sentences.zh: 我们现在已经量化了社交反馈，而在社交媒体出现之前，这种反馈要模糊得多。

sentences.en: Since humans are smart animals who learn quickly from feedback,
sentences.zh: 由于人类是能从反馈中快速学习的聪明动物，

sentences.en: we discover that there are very specific ways to get this delicious social approval.
sentences.zh: 我们发现了一些非常具体的方法来获得这种令人愉悦的社交认可。

sentences.en: My name is Jay Van Bevel.
sentences.zh: 我叫杰伊·范·贝维尔。

sentences.en: I'm a psychology professor at New York University.
sentences.zh: 我是纽约大学的心理学教授。

sentences.en: Jay and his team have analyzed more than half a million tweets.
sentences.zh: 杰伊和他的团队分析了超过五十万条推文。

sentences.en: He has found there is an easy way to dramatically increase likes and retweets.
sentences.zh: 他发现有一种简单的方法可以显著增加点赞和转发。

sentences.en: For every moral, emotional word that people use in a tweet,
sentences.zh: 对于人们在推文中使用的每一个道德、情感词汇，

sentences.en: we found that it increased the rate of retweeting from other people who saw it by 15 to 20 percent.
sentences.zh: 我们发现它能使看到该推文的其他人的转发率提高15%到20%。

sentences.en: Posts were retweeted 15 to 20 percent more if people used a moral or emotional word.
sentences.zh: 如果人们使用了道德或情感词汇，帖子被转发的几率会增加15%到20%。

sentences.en: The list of words that Jay and his colleagues defined as moral and emotional is quite long.
sentences.zh: 杰伊和他的同事定义的道德和情感词汇列表相当长。

sentences.en: Cursed words are on the list, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，诅咒词汇也在名单上。

sentences.en: Some other examples are words like hate, war, greed, punish.
sentences.zh: 其他一些例子包括仇恨、战争、贪婪、惩罚等词汇。

sentences.en: Jay read me some sample tweets.
sentences.zh: 杰伊给我读了一些推文样本。

sentences.en: So on the topic of same-sex marriage, here's an example tweet from a conservative.
sentences.zh: 关于同性婚姻的话题，这是一条来自保守派的推文示例。

sentences.en: Gay marriage is a diabolical, evil lie aimed at destroying our nation.
sentences.zh: 同性婚姻是一个旨在摧毁我们国家的邪恶、恶毒的谎言。

sentences.en: And the moral-emotional words here are evil and destroying.
sentences.zh: 这里的道德情感词汇是邪恶和摧毁。

sentences.en: And they're both negative, highly potent words.
sentences.zh: 它们都是负面的、极具影响力的词汇。

sentences.en: From a liberal, we have a tweet.
sentences.zh: 来自自由派的一条推文。

sentences.en: New Mormon policy bans children of same-sex parents.
sentences.zh: 新的摩门教政策禁止同性伴侣的孩子入教。

sentences.en: This church wants to punish children?
sentences.zh: 这个教会想要惩罚孩子？

sentences.en: Are you kidding me?
sentences.zh: 你在开玩笑吗？

sentences.en: Shame.
sentences.zh: 可耻。

sentences.en: You can also generate outrage without using those specific words, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，你也可以在不使用这些特定词汇的情况下引发愤怒。

sentences.en: you can say, can you believe she said that?
sentences.zh: 你可以说，你能相信她说了那种话吗？

sentences.en: Or, what kind of a country do we live in today?
sentences.zh: 或者，我们今天生活在什么样的国家里？

sentences.en: Jay's analysis didn't include tweets like that.
sentences.zh: 杰伊的分析没有包括这类推文。

sentences.en: But even using his more conservative measure,
sentences.zh: 但即使使用他更保守的衡量标准，

sentences.en: Jay found that moral and emotional words caused messages to spread.
sentences.zh: 杰伊发现道德和情感词汇确实促使了信息传播。

sentences.en: And you can, you know, jam a lot of words that have moral emotions in them in a single message
sentences.zh: 而且你可以在一条信息中塞进很多带有道德情感的词汇，

sentences.en: and increase the likelihood your message is going to be shared by 60 or 80 or 100 percent.
sentences.zh: 并将你的信息被分享的可能性提高60%、80%甚至100%。

sentences.en: This outrage often begets more outrage.
sentences.zh: 这种愤怒往往会招致更多的愤怒。

sentences.en: Twitter is weird because, you know, there's a level of outrage.
sentences.zh: 推特很奇怪，因为，你知道，存在一种愤怒的层级。

sentences.en: Then you have people who are outraged about the outrage
sentences.zh: 然后你会看到有人对这种愤怒感到愤怒，

sentences.en: because it's the wrong type of outrage.
sentences.zh: 因为他们认为这是错误的愤怒类型。

sentences.en: Then you have people who are outraged about that outrage.
sentences.zh: 然后又有人对那种愤怒感到愤怒。

sentences.en: And then you have another group of people who are outraged
sentences.zh: 接着还有另一群人感到愤怒，

sentences.en: that you're not outraged enough.
sentences.zh: 因为你愤怒得还不够。

sentences.en: So you have these four forms of outrage going on at any given time,
sentences.zh: 所以你在任何时候都会看到这四种形式的愤怒同时存在，

sentences.en: and it just cycles through issue after issue on a 24-hour basis.
sentences.zh: 并且它在24小时内不断地在各种议题之间循环。

sentences.en: To be sure, outrage sometimes produces real change.
sentences.zh: 可以肯定的是，愤怒有时确实会产生真正的改变。

sentences.en: It can bring together marginalized communities.
sentences.zh: 它可以将边缘化群体团结在一起。

sentences.en: It can fuel social movements such as the Arab Spring or Black Lives Matter.
sentences.zh: 它可以推动社会运动，如阿拉伯之春或“黑人的命也是命”。

sentences.en: It can help win elections.
sentences.zh: 它可以帮助赢得选举。

sentences.en: Outrage can be especially effective if your goal is to pull someone down.
sentences.zh: 如果你的目标是把某人拉下马，愤怒可能特别有效。

sentences.en: After all, this might be what the emotion was designed for in the first place.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，这可能就是这种情绪最初被设计出来的目的。

sentences.en: Today, Al Franken took to the mic as his political career came crashing down.
sentences.zh: 今天，阿尔·弗兰肯在政治生涯崩溃之际走上了麦克风。

sentences.en: I will be resigning as a member of the United States Senate.
sentences.zh: 我将辞去美国参议员的职务。

sentences.en: His resignation came after a number of his colleagues called for him to go.
sentences.zh: 在他辞职之前，许多同事呼吁他离开。

sentences.en: In an apology video posted on Twitter, Kathy Griffin is begging for forgiveness
sentences.zh: 在推特上发布的一段道歉视频中，凯西·格里芬在乞求原谅，

sentences.en: after images of her holding the stunning Oscar news overnight.
sentences.zh: 此前她手持奥斯卡惊人新闻的图片在网上流传。

sentences.en: Kevin Hart stepping down as hoSt.
sentences.zh: 凯文·哈特辞去主持人职务。

sentences.en: This came just days after his name was announced,
sentences.zh: 这距离他被宣布担任该职位仅过了几天，

sentences.en: and, of course, after a firestorm over past anti-gay tweets.
sentences.zh: 当然，这是在过去反同性恋推文引发轩然大波之后发生的。

sentences.en: Coming up, what outrage does not do well
sentences.zh: 接下来，我们将探讨愤怒不擅长做的事情，

sentences.en: and how to deploy fury more effectively.
sentences.zh: 以及如何更有效地运用愤怒。

sentences.en: It can feel good to start a fire,
sentences.zh: 点燃一把火感觉确实不错，

sentences.en: to see all the push notifications that come to your phone
sentences.zh: 看着手机上不断弹出的推送通知，

sentences.en: as people like and retweet your outrage.
sentences.zh: 人们点赞并转发你的愤怒。

sentences.en: Studies show that the more outrage you demonstrate,
sentences.zh: 研究表明，你表现出的愤怒越多，

sentences.en: the more your message is likely to spread.
sentences.zh: 你的信息传播的可能性就越大。

sentences.en: But psychologist William Brady at Yale says there is a great paradox in the way outrage works.
sentences.zh: 但耶鲁大学的心理学家威廉·布雷迪表示，愤怒的运作方式存在一个巨大的悖论。

sentences.en: Outrage leads to engagement, but not always to change.
sentences.zh: 愤怒能带来参与度，但并不总是能带来改变。

sentences.en: The type of people you're getting to that is giving you the shares and the likes,
sentences.zh: 那些给你分享和点赞的人，

sentences.en: it tends to be people who share your political views, so people of the same political ideology.
sentences.zh: 往往是那些与你政治观点相同的人，也就是具有相同政治意识形态的人。

sentences.en: In other words, outrage is very effective at spreading a message within an echo chamber.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，愤怒在回声壁内传播信息非常有效。

sentences.en: The use of outrage, the use of moral and emotional language on social media,
sentences.zh: 在社交媒体上使用愤怒，使用道德和情感语言，

sentences.en: it really depends on the context and what you're trying to accomplish.
sentences.zh: 这真的取决于语境以及你想要达成什么目标。

sentences.en: If you want to rally the troops, get my people who already agree with me
sentences.zh: 如果你想集结队伍，让那些已经同意我观点的人，

sentences.en: to get interested and to get motivated to act,
sentences.zh: 对某事感兴趣并被激励去采取行动，

sentences.en: or is it really to try to persuade others?
sentences.zh: 还是说你真的想去说服其他人？

sentences.en: If your goal is the former,
sentences.zh: 如果你的目标是前者，

sentences.en: then expressing yourself with moral emotions like outrage can be really effective.
sentences.zh: 那么用愤怒这种道德情感来表达自己是非常有效的。

sentences.en: If your goal is the latter, then perhaps it's not the best idea.
sentences.zh: 如果你的目标是后者，那么这可能不是最好的主意。

sentences.en: In a study that William has conducted with J.
sentences.zh: 在威廉与杰伊·范·贝维尔共同进行的一项研究中，

sentences.en: Van Bevel,
sentences.zh: 他发现，没有道德和情感色彩的推文，

sentences.en: he found that tweets without a moral and emotional tone
sentences.zh: 更能开启对话，

sentences.en: were better able to start conversations
sentences.zh: 促进不同政治立场的人之间的交流。

sentences.en: between people from different political persuasions.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，这符合直觉。

sentences.en: In some ways, this makes intuitive sense.
sentences.zh: 你上一次改变主意，

sentences.en: When was the last time you changed your mind
sentences.zh: 是因为有人对你大吼大叫是什么时候？

sentences.en: because someone screamed at you?
sentences.zh: 因为有人对你大吼大叫是什么时候？

sentences.en: And that leads to an interesting question.
sentences.zh: 这引出了一个有趣的问题。

sentences.en: Why do we still see so much outrage
sentences.zh: 为什么我们仍然看到如此多的愤怒

sentences.en: even when we know that it causes the people who disagree with us to tune us out.
sentences.zh: 即使我们知道这会导致那些与我们意见相左的人不再听我们说话。

sentences.en: Aren't those precisely the people whose minds we want to change?
sentences.zh: 难道这些人不正是我们想要改变想法的对象吗？

sentences.en: Molly Crockett thinks there's a reason beyond our own personal motivations.
sentences.zh: 莫莉·克罗克特认为，除了我们个人的动机之外，还有一个原因。

sentences.en: It has to do with the business models of social media platforms and broadcast outlets.
sentences.zh: 这与社交媒体平台和广播媒体的商业模式有关。

sentences.en: The goal of the platforms is not the explicit goal of keeping us outraged.
sentences.zh: 这些平台的明确目标并不是为了让我们保持愤怒。

sentences.en: It just happens to be that outrage is one way to grab attention and increase engagement.
sentences.zh: 只是恰好愤怒是吸引注意力和增加参与度的一种方式。

sentences.en: And their goal is engagement and holding our attention as much as possible
sentences.zh: 而他们的目标是参与度，并尽可能地抓住我们的注意力

sentences.en: because that's what's monetized in the business model of the social media platforMs.
sentences.zh: 因为这就是社交媒体平台商业模式中实现货币化的东西。

sentences.en: The private benefits of outrage do not flow only to big companies.
sentences.zh: 愤怒带来的私人利益并不仅仅流向大公司。

sentences.en: Increasingly, pundits, commentators, and social media influencers
sentences.zh: 越来越多的权威人士、评论员和社交媒体网红

sentences.en: users use their visibility to drive advertising, book sales, and brand development.
sentences.zh: 用户利用他们的曝光度来推动广告、图书销售和品牌发展。

sentences.en: There is a new number one atop the New York Times bestseller list, Tucker Carlson's Ship
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》畅销书排行榜上出现了一位新的冠军，塔克·卡尔森的《愚人船》

sentences.en: of Fools, unseating Bob Woodward's fear, Trump and the White House.
sentences.zh: 取代了鲍勃·伍德沃德的《恐惧：特朗普在白宫》。

sentences.en: What motivated you to write this book?
sentences.zh: 是什么促使你写这本书的？

sentences.en: Well, you know, during the 2016 election, I was noticing the level of anger.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，在2016年大选期间，我注意到了那种愤怒的程度。

sentences.en: You like my shirt, guys?
sentences.zh: 伙计们，你们喜欢我的衬衫吗？

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，喜欢。

sentences.en: Shoptyt.com.
sentences.zh: Shoptyt.com.

sentences.en: And if you haven't ordered it yet or you haven't picked it up, make sure you do that.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没订购或者还没买到，一定要去买。

sentences.en: It's a great Fourth of July read.
sentences.zh: 这是一本非常适合在独立日阅读的书。

sentences.en: These private incentives explain why the well for outrage runs deep,
sentences.zh: 这些私人激励机制解释了为什么愤怒的源泉如此深厚，

sentences.en: why there are new things to be outraged about every hour of every day.
sentences.zh: 为什么每天每小时都有新的事情让人愤怒。

sentences.en: While this makes excellent sense for the business models of influencers and their media platforms,
sentences.zh: 虽然这对网红及其媒体平台的商业模式来说非常有意义，

sentences.en: Molly says it does not make much sense for the rest of us.
sentences.zh: 但莫莉说，这对我们其他人来说并没有太大意义。

sentences.en: It's just constant.
sentences.zh: 这简直是没完没了。

sentences.en: There's a constant drip feed of outrage.
sentences.zh: 愤怒在不断地滴灌式输入。

sentences.en: and it makes it hard to know where to focus your efforts.
sentences.zh: 这让人很难知道该把精力集中在哪里。

sentences.en: At a certain point, audiences start to become numb.
sentences.zh: 在某个时刻，受众开始变得麻木。

sentences.en: If you were supposed to be angry about one thing on Monday
sentences.zh: 如果你周一应该对某件事感到愤怒

sentences.en: and another on Tuesday, by Wednesday, you're exhausted.
sentences.zh: 周二又对另一件事感到愤怒，到了周三，你就精疲力竭了。

sentences.en: You may start to tune things out.
sentences.zh: 你可能会开始屏蔽这些信息。

sentences.en: You can't prioritize what to care about
sentences.zh: 你无法分清什么才是真正值得关心的

sentences.en: because the volume on everything is turned to 11.
sentences.zh: 因为所有事情的音量都被调到了最大。

sentences.en: In the process, things that actually need our attention, where the volume needs to be turned to 11, are drowned out.
sentences.zh: 在这个过程中，那些真正需要我们关注、真正需要调大音量的事情，反而被淹没了。

sentences.en: Careful vetting and investigative reporting today are regularly overshadowed by incendiary opinion.
sentences.zh: 如今，严谨的审查和调查报道经常被煽动性的观点所掩盖。

sentences.en: A similar dynamic is playing out in many parts of the world.
sentences.zh: 类似的动态正在世界许多地方上演。

sentences.en: In Britain, about two-thirds of people say they no longer can tell the difference between rumor and reporting.
sentences.zh: 在英国，大约三分之二的人表示他们已经无法分辨谣言和新闻报道的区别了。

sentences.en: If you're dialing up the volume on all outrage, then it may become more difficult to detect
sentences.zh: 如果你把所有愤怒的音量都调大，那么可能就更难检测出

sentences.en: signal in an increasingly noisy public sphere.
sentences.zh: 在日益嘈杂的公共领域中的真实信号。

sentences.en: And this could increase errors that we make in
sentences.zh: 这可能会增加我们在以下方面的错误判断：

sentences.en: deciding which issues we collectively think are most worthy of our attention and support.
sentences.zh: 决定哪些议题是我们集体认为最值得关注和支持的。

sentences.en: Molly Crockett and William Brady are studying whether outrage might also be counterproductive to activists.
sentences.zh: 莫莉·克罗克特和威廉·布雷迪正在研究愤怒是否也可能对活动人士产生反作用。

sentences.en: Does blasting out angry tweets cause some people to feel they have done their part,
sentences.zh: 发布愤怒的推文是否会让一些人觉得他们已经尽了自己的责任，

sentences.en: to forego the more difficult challenges of protesting in public, driving legislation, or showing up to vote?
sentences.zh: 从而放弃了更困难的挑战，比如公开抗议、推动立法或参加投票？

sentences.en: In other words, can outrage foster slacktivism?
sentences.zh: 换句话说，愤怒能助长“键盘侠”行为吗？

sentences.en: I think that's a genuine worry.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个真正的担忧。

sentences.en: I don't think we have the data to know for sure.
sentences.zh: 我不认为我们有足够的数据来确定这一点。

sentences.en: But it is a possibility and it is something we should worry about because if you're a certain type of person and maybe you only have enough time to take one action and not do both,
sentences.zh: 但这是一种可能性，也是我们应该担心的事情，因为如果你是某种类型的人，也许你只有足够的时间采取一种行动，而不能两者兼顾，

sentences.en: then maybe expressing outrage because it is less costly on social media is what you end up doing.
sentences.zh: 那么也许在社交媒体上表达愤怒因为成本更低，就成了你最终的选择。

sentences.en: and then you don't actually go and you don't actually protest,
sentences.zh: 然后你实际上并没有去行动，也没有去抗议，

sentences.en: you don't actually put pressure on legislators
sentences.zh: 你实际上并没有向立法者施压，

sentences.en: like what is really needed to create concrete change.
sentences.zh: 而这才是创造具体变革真正需要的。

sentences.en: For her part, Julie Zimmerman says her experience
sentences.zh: 就她而言，朱莉·齐默尔曼说她的经历

sentences.en: has changed the way she feeds off outrage.
sentences.zh: 改变了她从愤怒中汲取能量的方式。

sentences.en: If you can limit yourself to just those occasional check-ins,
sentences.zh: 如果你能把自己限制在偶尔查看一下，

sentences.en: a lot of the stories that are wasting people's time
sentences.zh: 很多浪费人们时间的报道

sentences.en: have gone away by the next time you sign on.
sentences.zh: 等你下次登录时就已经消失了。

sentences.en: She's also decided to refocus her emotional energy.
sentences.zh: 她还决定重新调整自己的情感能量。

sentences.en: You can stand up and be super outraged about something national,
sentences.zh: 你可以站出来，对全国性的事情感到超级愤怒，

sentences.en: but if you really want to have an impact,
sentences.zh: 但如果你真的想产生影响，

sentences.en: yeah, go pick up litter in the intersection near your house
sentences.zh: 是的，去清理你家附近十字路口的垃圾，

sentences.en: or go work at an animal shelter.
sentences.zh: 或者去动物收容所工作。

sentences.en: There are things that we can do every day
sentences.zh: 我们每天都可以做一些事情，

sentences.en: that improve our lives and the lives of people around us,
sentences.zh: 改善我们的生活以及周围人的生活，

sentences.en: but they don't give us that, you know, that drug of having a hot take spread around social media.
sentences.zh: 但它们不会给我们那种，你知道的，那种在社交媒体上传播热门观点所带来的快感。

sentences.en: We tell ourselves, well, we're being good citizens.
sentences.zh: 我们告诉自己，嗯，我们是好公民。

sentences.en: We're keeping up on the news.
sentences.zh: 我们在关注新闻。

sentences.en: We're just entertaining ourselves, you know, at great expense to our society.
sentences.zh: 我们只是在娱乐自己，你知道的，以牺牲我们的社会为代价。

sentences.en: So many tools of modern culture take ancient circuits in the brain and put them in hyperdrive.
sentences.zh: 现代文化的许多工具利用大脑中古老的回路，并让它们超速运转。

sentences.en: We evolved to need nutrition, but many of us are surrounded by so much food that we now get sick.
sentences.zh: 我们进化到需要营养，但我们许多人被如此多的食物包围，以至于现在生病了。

sentences.en: We evolved to care about relationships, but social media has weaponized this,
sentences.zh: 我们进化到关心人际关系，但社交媒体已经将其武器化，

sentences.en: transforming personal connections into metrics of self-worth.
sentences.zh: 将个人联系转化为自我价值的衡量标准。

sentences.en: Getting angry at wrongdoers was helpful in our evolutionary paSt.
sentences.zh: 在我们的进化史上，对作恶者感到愤怒是有帮助的。

sentences.en: But when people apply that same impulse today on talk radio and Twitter,
sentences.zh: 但当人们今天在谈话广播和推特上应用同样的冲动时，

sentences.en: what we get are doxing and death threats.
sentences.zh: 我们得到的是人肉搜索和死亡威胁。

sentences.en: Our capacity for outrage, honed over millennia, gives our society guardrails.
sentences.zh: 我们经过数千年磨练出来的愤怒能力，为我们的社会提供了护栏。

sentences.en: It tells us how we are supposed to behave, and it can lead to positive change.
sentences.zh: 它告诉我们应该如何行事，并且可以带来积极的改变。

sentences.en: But used recklessly or for self-promotion, outrage can poison the way we interact with each other.
sentences.zh: 但如果鲁莽使用或用于自我推销，愤怒会毒害我们彼此互动的方式。

sentences.en: It can imprison us in our own echo chambers.
sentences.zh: 它会把我们囚禁在自己的回声室里。

sentences.zh: 想了解更多《Hidden Brain》的内容，你可以在 Facebook、Twitter 和 hiddenbrain.org 上关注我们。
